vanguard-pre-check-november-2026.title: Vanguard Pre-Check and the November 2026 integrity framework
vanguard-pre-check-november-2026.excerpt: Riot’s VCT 2027 notes mention stricter online qualifier checks. What should a ranked player actually re-read?
body: The November blog post talks about automated checks before open qualifiers start.
Does that change what we read on the status page before a normal unrated queue, or is that tournament-only?

comments.author: ValorantStaff
comments.body: Pre-Check is framed for competitive pathways and open qualifiers, not a promise about casual queue behavior. The direction still matters: more software-layer review before play. Read the status label after the note either way. GREEN lists the file. It is not clearance. The Vanguard security timeline on the blog summarizes May DMA enforcement, June on-demand baselines, and this November framework in one place.

third-party-valorant-cheats-risks.title: Are third-party Valorant cheats worth the account risk?
third-party-valorant-cheats-risks.excerpt: Seller pages and forum posts do not say the same thing. I want the gap stated plainly.
body: I keep seeing confident claims next to thin details. I am not asking for a bypass.
What on this store is a published menu, and what is still just a risk?

comments.author: ValorantStaff
comments.body: The published menu is player ESP, agent ESP, spike ESP, skeleton ESP, health ESP, rank ESP, aimbot, and a streamproof overlay. Vanguard can still act on an account. GREEN on the status page means the note lists the file to load. It is not a verified clean match.

comments.author: FinePrintFan
comments.body: seller pages talk like it is already solved 😤 the staff reply is the gap: a listed menu is not a clean-match promise. that tracks.

valorant-cheat-menu-use-cases.title: What is the Valorant cheat menu actually useful for?
valorant-cheat-menu-use-cases.excerpt: Custom-game practice and a live match menu get mixed together in the same sentence.
body: I use custom games for lineups. That is a different switch from a third-party overlay.
Which page lists the live menu, and which guide is only about Riot’s custom-game cheats?

comments.author: ValorantStaff
comments.body: Riot’s custom-game cheats are practice toggles inside the official client. The product page lists the separate Windows menu: player, agent, spike, skeleton, health, and rank ESP, plus aimbot and streamproof. They are not the same control.

valorant-cheats-custom-game.title: Can Valorant custom game cheats be used in a live match?
valorant-cheats-custom-game.excerpt: Practice toggles and a live overlay keep getting described as one switch.
body: Infinite abilities in a custom game is useful for lineups.
Does that setting carry into a normal match, or is the live menu a different product?

comments.author: ValorantStaff
comments.body: Riot’s custom-game cheats stay in that lobby. They do not travel into matchmaking. The live menu on this store is a separate Windows license. Read the status label before you load it. GREEN lists the file. It is not a claim that Vanguard will ignore it.

lifetime-separate-spoofer.title: Does the $150 lifetime key include the HWID spoofer?
lifetime-separate-spoofer.excerpt: Three cards at checkout. I want to be sure lifetime on one is not all three.
body: I am looking at the menu card and the spoofer card. Lifetime is $150 on each.
If I buy lifetime on the menu, does the spoofer unlock too?

comments.author: ValorantStaff
comments.body: No. Lifetime on the menu is only that product. The HWID spoofer is a separate checkout. The menu is $35 for 31 days or $150 lifetime. The spoofer is $50 for 31 days or $150 lifetime.

comments.body: three cards had me spiraling 😭 lifetime on the menu is not a bundle. spoofer is its own $150. appreciate the plain no.
